title: Turkey Forces Google to Let News Sites Exit AI Overviews
summary: Turkey mandates Google allow publishers to opt out of AI Overviews while staying in search results, setting a global precedent for AI content control.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Turkey has forced Google to implement controls letting news sites opt out of AI Overviews while remaining in traditional search results.
- The regulation marks the first government mandate requiring separate opt-out mechanisms for AI features versus standard search indexing globally.
- Publishers can now block their content from generative AI summaries without sacrificing organic search visibility and traffic on Google.


Turkey has mandated that Google implement technical controls allowing news publishers to opt out of AI Overviews while maintaining their presence in traditional search results. Officially launched on November 22, 2026, this regulatory intervention represents the first government-enforced separation of AI feature participation from core search indexing, challenging Google's previous bundled approach to content access.


## The Regulatory Mandate


Turkey's competition authority issued the directive after publishers complained that Google's existing robots.txt controls forced an all-or-nothing choice: either allow content in both search results and AI Overviews, or disappear from Google entirely. The new requirement compels Google to honor a separate opt-out mechanism specifically for generative AI features while preserving standard search visibility. According to sources familiar with the directive, Google has 60 days to implement the technical infrastructure within Turkey's jurisdiction.


The decision follows months of pressure from Turkish news organizations arguing that AI Overviews extract and summarize their content without adequate attribution or traffic compensation. By mandating granular control, regulators aim to protect publisher revenue streams while maintaining public access to information through traditional search.


## How the Split Opt-Out Works


Under the new framework, publishers can deploy targeted meta tags or configuration files that specifically exclude their content from AI-generated summaries and overviews. These controls operate independently from the standard noindex directives that govern search engine crawling. Key implementation details include:


- A new meta tag that blocks AI feature inclusion without affecting search ranking signals
- Separate robots.txt entries distinguishing between traditional crawlers and AI training or summary systems
- Publisher dashboard controls within[Google Search Console](https://emergent.sh/news/google-search-console-mcp-now-available) for managing AI visibility preferences


Google has not publicly confirmed whether these technical solutions will extend beyond Turkey or remain jurisdiction-specific. Industry observers expect other regions to monitor Turkey's experiment closely as a potential regulatory template.


## Publisher and Industry Reactions


Turkish news organizations have welcomed the mandate as a critical protection for digital journalism business models. Several major publishers reported that AI Overviews reduced click-through rates by 20 to 35 percent for certain query types, as users consumed summarized information without visiting source websites. The ability to reclaim that traffic while maintaining search presence offers a middle path between total visibility and complete withdrawal.


Meanwhile, Google has issued measured statements emphasizing its commitment to working with regulators while noting that AI Overviews already include prominent source links and attribution. The company has not indicated whether voluntary opt-out controls might eventually be offered globally, independent of regulatory pressure.


## What This Means


Turkey's directive establishes a legal precedent that could reshape how platforms balance AI innovation with content creator rights worldwide. If the split opt-out model proves effective without degrading user experience, other governments may adopt similar mandates. For publishers, the policy offers a testing ground to measure the true traffic and revenue impact of AI-generated summaries. For Google, the requirement adds complexity to content management systems but may ultimately provide a framework for navigating ongoing tensions between AI features and the open web ecosystem that powers them.
